clue.text: Large glasses being provided, sat and drank freely

indicators.note: drank freely suggests unrestrained drinking, but it tells us the letters of sat and drank are free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sits down and drinks heavily once the big glasses are handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges SAT and DRANK, the words around 'and', into the eight letters needed; 'being provided' and 'and' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large drinking mugs, often pewter or glass, with handles, used for beer.

clue.text: Quarrel involving painter turning up for duties

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for painter is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword painter

explanation.surface: An argument with an artist who rebels over taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes AR from RA, and 'involving' sets it inside TIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a list of import or export duties levied by a government.

clue.text: Ship in sodium and gold for a place in the Bahamas

indicators.note: the word for ship is placed within the chemical symbols that follow

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
SS, steamship, is a ship

explanation.surface: A vessel loaded with salt and bullion bound for a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SS inside NA + AU.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of the Bahamas, on New Providence island.

clue.text: They're cold-blooded and they're calculating

explanation.surface: A description of ruthless, scheming people.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves seem to describe the same heartless schemers; one is snakes, the other is people or machines that do sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Vipers are cold-blooded reptiles; also, those who add up figures are calculating.

clue.text: Part of a building where people take courses

definitions.text: Part of a building where people take courses

parts.words: Part of a building where people take courses
parts.note: courses sound like lessons at a college, but they are the courses of a meal, eaten in a household room

explanation.definitionFit: It is the room in a house where meals of several courses are eaten.

clue.text: Not now to be found in a southern Greek city

indicators.note: the phrase says one piece sits inside the letters that follow it in the clue

parts.note: a time that is not now is then

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a thing once present in a southern Greek city is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be found in' puts THEN inside A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital of Greece and its most famous ancient city.

clue.text: Set items out all higgledy-piggledy and get the bird

indicators.note: to set things out can mean to lay them out afresh, one hint that the letters are rearranged
higgledy-piggledy means in confused disorder, so the letters of items out are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone scatters things messily and is jeered for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' and 'all higgledy-piggledy' both say to rearrange ITEMS OUT. 'Get the bird' is slang for being booed, but here the bird is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A titmouse is a small songbird, another name for a tit.

clue.text: Once quietly keeping within the law, that's plain

parts.note: ex means former, once
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: Someone who once stayed quietly law-abiding is being clear about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' only joins here.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit statements are clear and plain, leaving nothing implied.

clue.text: The lowest class will find the boards accommodating always

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: the boards is the stage of a theatre
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Poor passengers are always housed in the cheapest deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts EER inside STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: On a passenger ship, the cheapest accommodation was the steerage section.

clue.text: Living with division restricting the players

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one word's letters close around the other's

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear, a division
the players in a game form a side, a team

explanation.surface: Life with a split that hampers the members of a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' puts SIDE inside RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resident somewhere is dwelling there, as in 'resident in Paris'.

clue.text: Plates — fancy or quite basic

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, signalling the letters of plates are made over

explanation.surface: A choice between decorative crockery and something plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges PLATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple item is a basic, standard one, like bread or rice in a diet.

clue.text: Glaring when making standard bombastic speech

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
a rant is a loud, overblown tirade

explanation.surface: Someone glares while delivering a pompous oration about the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant error is a conspicuous, obvious one, just as a glaring error is.

clue.text: There's firm support for modern office equipment

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
a pier is a pillar that supports a bridge or building

explanation.surface: A claim that some office machine stands on solid foundations.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopying machine is a fixture of the modern office.

clue.text: Tradesmen start and one is in chaos!

indicators.note: chaos means utter disorder, so the letters of start and one is are thrown about

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers begin trading and one of them is overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in chaos' rearranges START and ONE IS; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationers are shopkeepers who sell paper, pens and similar writing goods.

clue.text: In favour of trying, though raising some objection

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
testing, like trying, means putting something to the test; both can also mean taxing

explanation.surface: Someone supports an attempt yet still voices a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To be complaining or objecting is to be voicing a protest.

clue.text: Observing cannabis in smart environs

indicators.note: environs are the surroundings, so the word for smart surrounds the other

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Seeing someone with cannabis in a fashionable neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective, smart environs being a posh area, but it is a verb meaning sting; 'environs' puts POT inside STING.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting is seeing or noticing, as in train-spotting.

clue.text: No charge imposed for cargo space in this property

indicators.note: imposed means placed on top, so in this down clue the first word sits above the second

parts.note: free means costing nothing
a ship's hold is where cargo is stored

explanation.surface: A landlord adds a fee for storage space at this estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A freehold is a form of property ownership held outright and indefinitely.

clue.text: Get away without a small daughter and frolic

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the first word stands around the letters that follow

parts.note: to escape is to get away
D is the short form of daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A girl slips away alone for some fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, putting A and D inside ESCAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a lively, mischievous adventure, a frolic.

clue.text: Turns left, taking the outlet for a coastal town

parts.note: to port the helm is a nautical verb meaning to turn a ship to the left
the mouth of a river is where it flows out to the sea

explanation.surface: A sailor steers left and heads out through the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT is the left side of a ship, and as a verb it means to turn that way; 'taking' only joins. PORTSMOUTH is a naval port on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A Royal Navy base and city on England's south coast, facing the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: An oarsman must be fit

explanation.surface: A rower needs to be in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like an adjective meaning healthy, but it is a noun: a sudden attack of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, the stroke sets the pace for the crew; and a stroke is a sudden seizure, a fit.

clue.text: Sausage eaten by Italians as mail is sorted

indicators.note: mail is sorted at a post office; sorting here puts the letters of as mail into a new order

explanation.surface: Italians eat a sausage as the post is being sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is sorted' rearranges AS MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spicy Italian sausage.

clue.text: Ring, not for the first time, to make a cancellation

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: Calling again to cancel an arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a' only joins; 'not for the first time' gives the prefix meaning again, placed before PEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeal is the revoking of a law, its cancellation.

clue.text: The prohibition that's of ancient Egyptian origin

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a certain ban dates back to pharaonic Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt (there is also a Greek Thebes), so its adjective fits an Egyptian origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from Thebes, the ancient Egyptian capital on the Nile, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: The face of the cockney — causing a big row

explanation.surface: A Londoner's expression gives rise to a heated argument.
explanation.walkthrough: In cockney rhyming slang 'boat race' means face. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames, a big 'row' in the oar sense, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang pairs the phrase with face; separately, it names the famous university rowing contest.

clue.text: A line on a chart is nothing to the legal profession

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing
the Bar is the collective name for barristers, the legal profession

explanation.surface: A remark that a mere line on a chart means nothing to lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, a curve joining points of equal atmospheric pressure is such a line.

clue.text: Notes are arranged so they echo

indicators.note: musical notes are arranged by a composer; here the letters of the words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Musical notes are scored so that they reverberate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges NOTES and ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring or reverberate with sound is to echo.

clue.text: State the minister and newsman gallivanted together

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a minister's degree
ED, short for editor, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A politician and a journalist went out on the town together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning 'say', but it is a US state; 'the', 'and' and 'together' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about is to roam idly in search of pleasure, which is gallivanting.

clue.text: Remarkable pieces fashioned by a trainee

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped or made, so the letters of pieces are worked into a new form

parts.note: L, for learner, marks a trainee driver

explanation.surface: Notable items made by an apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges PIECES into ESPECI, then A and L (the learner driver's plate) follow.
explanation.definitionFit: This rather formal adjective means exceptional or particular, out of the ordinary.
